entry.title: Acer Unveils Predator Atlas 7 Handheld Gaming Device
entry.content:
Techmeme | engadget.com | source

Acer has announced the Predator Atlas 7 handheld gaming device at the IFA conference in Berlin. The device provides the same performance as the larger Atlas 8, utilizing up to an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor and Intel Arc B390 graphics. It includes a 7-inch 120 Hz FHD touchscreen protected by Corning Gorilla Glass Victus and features contoured grips and an enlarged palm rest for improved ergonomics.

The device is available with an 80Wh battery, weighing under 750g, or a 60Wh battery, weighing under 700g. It includes dual Thunderbolt 4 ports, a microSD card reader, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 5.4. Acer expects a North American release in the fourth quarter of 2026 and an EMEA release in November.

entry.title: Dwarf Fortress Creator Criticizes Industry Focus on AI and Layoffs
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | pcgamer.com | hacker news

Tarn Adams, co-founder of Bay 12 Games and creator of Dwarf Fortress, has criticized the video game industry's reliance on generative AI and frequent layoffs. Speaking at Gamescom 2026, Adams argued that executive-led efforts to automate development are unsustainable and fail to account for the complexity required for high-quality game creation.

Adams suggested that prioritizing AI-driven efficiency over skilled labor could eventually trigger a market reckoning as the consumer base is impacted by unemployment. He also noted a semantic shift in the industry, such as the move toward describing "dwarf behavior" instead of "dwarf AI," as an example of the confusion surrounding the technology.

entry.title: Former id Software Producer Reports Severe Crunch for Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Andrew Willis, a former producer at id Software, reports that much of the Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC was developed in a concentrated period of only three to four months. During this time, staff faced extreme working hours, with Willis reporting shifts of up to 17 hours and weekly 80-hour workloads.

This development period occurred alongside significant layoffs at id Software and Xbox, which impacted approximately 136 employees. Willis described the environment as "pseudo-induced crunch," where developers felt compelled to work extreme overtime to meet high quality standards despite the absence of explicit management mandates.

entry.title: Aggro Crab Launches New Publishing Label
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Aggro Crab, the developer of Another Crab's Treasure and Peak, has launched a new publishing label called Aggro Crab Presents. The initiative is designed to support indie game projects with budgets up to $500,000 that are expected to launch within two years. The studio has already signed its first two projects: Rebounder by ThirtyThree and Subway Midnight by Bubby Darkstar.

Following the success of Peak, the publishing arm will focus on "stylized games with an attitude" and will not accept titles using generative AI. Aggro Crab intends to offer flexible contract terms, including adjustable milestones and revenue models that avoid 100% recoupment to ensure developers maintain cash flow.

The decision follows reports that player retention for the hybrid runner and card collection game failed to meet expectations. This closure follows a series of restructuring efforts at Rovio since its 2023 acquisition by Sega, which included the closure of Studio Lumi and various rounds of layoffs.

entry.title: Nvidia to Launch DLSS 5 for RTX 50-Series GPUs
entry.content:
Techmeme | theverge.com | source

Nvidia will launch DLSS 5 on September 3, providing "3D-Guided Neural Rendering" for RTX 50-series desktop and laptop GPUs and GeForce NOW. The technology uses AI to enhance real-time lighting and textures, and NBA 2K27 will be the first game to feature official support.

The feature has faced criticism for its potential to significantly alter character appearances in early demonstrations. Additionally, the technology carries a substantial performance cost, with estimates suggesting a 50% to 60% reduction in frame rates.

entry.title: Paradox Interactive's Afterworld Integrates RPG Elements to Attract Grand Strategy Players
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Paradox Development Studio's Afterworld is a post-apocalyptic grand strategy game designed to expand the genre's reach through role-playing mechanics. Set in a rebuilding North America, players lead tribes that evolve via a dynamic "Ideas Tree," which unlocks social structures and technologies based on specific environmental discoveries.

Game director Dan Lind aims to ease players into the genre by prioritizing tribal backstories and emergent storytelling over complex historical starting points. This design allows players to define their own goals and shape their tribe's cultural identity through exploration and survival.

Bit Reactor, the developer of the tactical combat game Star Wars Zero Company, confirmed it furloughed a significant number of workers prior to the title's August 27, 2026, release. The studio told Game File the decision to temporarily suspend employees without pay was made due to uncertainty regarding the game's launch performance.

Sources suggest the furloughs may have impacted as much as 80 percent of the Bit Reactor team, leaving a skeleton crew to manage post-launch support. While the EA-published title has reached bestseller status on Steam, former employees have alleged that the studio's actions included cutting staff off from profit-sharing and providing misleading information regarding their employment status.

entry.title: ASCII City Prototype Developed with Custom JavaScript Engine
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | youtube.com | hacker news

A raycasting-based engine renders a three-dimensional urban environment using only ASCII characters on an HTML5 canvas. This prototype maps a grid-based world of roads, buildings, vehicles, and pedestrians into a character-based visual field without the use of 3D models or textures.

The system determines character size, brightness, and perspective based on ray-hit distance and depth. This implementation also manages occlusion and basic collision detection to simulate an inhabited environment within a single HTML file.

entry.title: Gamescom Equipment Thefts Target Indie Developers and Publishers
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Multiple independent developers and publishers, including Tessera Studios and iam8bit, reported the theft of laptops and Steam Decks from their booths during Gamescom 2026. The incidents occurred in the general business area and the Indie Arena, with some victims reporting the loss of devices containing critical company and personal information.

Gamescom organizers stated that while general security is provided, exhibitors are responsible for individual stand security and should insure their equipment. This response has faced industry criticism, especially amid allegations from Ukiyo Studios that organizers have previously discouraged filing police reports to protect the event's and the city's reputation.

entry.title: Steam2 Teraleak Exposes Decades of Lost Valve and Third-Party Game Content
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | arstechnica.com | hacker news

A 12TB archive containing content from Valve’s defunct Steam2 server architecture has surfaced via a BitTorrent tracker. This collection includes thousands of "depots" encompassing public releases, pre-release builds, prototypes, and playtest versions of numerous titles from the period between 2003 and 2013. Data miners report that the files were likely obtained via a publicly accessible and unprotected API endpoint.

The leak features significant assets from major franchises, such as cut dialogue and mechanics from Portal 2 and files potentially related to a Half-Life 2: Episode 3 expansion. Beyond Valve's software, the archive contains early versions of third-party titles like Spore and Dragon Age: Origins. The event highlights both the potential for massive data loss in software lifecycles and the legal risks associated with the distribution of third-party intellectual property.

entry.title: Red Hook Studios Explains Art-Led Procedural Generation for Darkest Dungeon 2
entry.content:
GDC Videos | youtube.com | source

Red Hook Studios' Darkest Dungeon 2 utilizes an art-led procedural generation system to balance a specific visual style with gameplay replayability. To avoid the high labor costs and visual repetition of an initial "sequential plate" approach, the development team transitioned to a modular hex-based grid system.

This system generates interconnected nodes and branching paths that facilitate strategic decision-making. By using smaller tiles, the developers were able to increase visual variety and maintain the game's signature ink-heavy, painterly aesthetic across different biomes.

entry.title: OpenTIE Reimplementation of Star Wars: TIE Fighter for Windows, macOS, and Linux
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | github.com | hacker news

OpenTIE is an open-source reimplementation of Star Wars: TIE Fighter designed for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It runs original game data natively and allows users to combine assets from the 1995 Collector's CD-ROM and the 1998 Windows release, such as the 1995 adaptive iMUSE soundtrack and menus with the 1998 flight simulation.

Modernization features include ambient occlusion, bloom, HDR output, and AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1.4 upscaling. The software supports high-refresh-rate displays up to 240 Hz and provides compatibility for modern gamepads and joysticks.
